newsitem.title: UK: Aluminium producer stocks fall to four-year low.
newsitem.headline: Aluminium producer stocks fall to four-year low.

text.p: The latest hefty fall in producer aluminium stocks more than outweighs the rise in London Metal Exchange (LME) inventories this year, setting the stage for a turnaround in the market, a leading analyst said.
"This is the lowest level of total producer stocks since November 1992...It is a significant fall which the market will ignore at its peril," said analyst Nick Moore of Flemings Global Mining Group.

Total stocks at Western world aluminium smelters, excluding finished end-products, fell by 96,000 tonnes in September 1996 from the previous month, data by the International Primary Aluminium Institute (IPAI) showed on Monday.
This brought total stocks down to 3.257 million tonnes.
Since January 1996 producer stocks have dropped by 372,000 tonnes while LME stocks have risen over the same period by 321,000 tonnes, Moore said.
Considering that overall 1996 aluminium production is expected to rise by more than 900,000 tonnes over 1995, the latest data is a very positive sign, he added.
"This shows that the ship is finally turning. It shows that the market should not be too obsessed with just looking at LME stocks," he said.
Unwrought aluminium stocks fell to 1.747 million tonnes, the lowest level since March 1993.
LME three month prices showed little immediate reaction to the IPAI data in slow trading, holding little changed from earlier levels around $1,450 per tonne.
But the lower producer stocks should soon lead to drawdowns in LME stocks and feed through to the price, Moore said.
